title: Coding Activity YAML
description: Schema for a coding activity: an OpenAI-compatible coding endpoint an external coding agent (e.g. little-coder) points at. Kept in sync by hand with the Zod schema in lib/coding-schema.ts, which is the source of truth for validation.

id.description: Short machine-readable activity id, e.g. beginner-typescript.

name.description: Optional human-readable label (not shown to the student).

title.description: Optional label shown to the student on the /<code> connection page.

fragment_files.description: Optional fragment libraries this activity pulls shared prompt fragments from.

fragments.description: Optional fragments selected from fragment_files. Assembled in priority order and prepended AHEAD of instructions.

instructions.description: The assistant's system prompt. SERVER-ONLY: never sent to the browser or the coding agent, and appended AFTER the coding tool's own prompt (so the teacher has the final word). Constrain the assistant to what your class has learned.

model.description: The model that answers. SERVER-ONLY and PINNED: the proxy always uses this model and ignores whatever model the coding agent sends.

provider.description: The LLM provider serving the model. For Azure Foundry, model is the deployment name.

url.description: HTTP(S) URL or relative path to the fragment library.

id.description: Fragment id inside the referenced library.

variables.description: Literal values passed into the fragment template.

bind.description: Accepted for compatibility but ignored by the current assembler.

required.description: Marker for important fragments. Accepted but not currently enforced.
